question: How do you perform sajdat al-sahw, the prostration of forgetfulness?
answer:
Because it's rapid fire, we're going to be doing this very quickly. Do realize that this topic is one where you will find a vast spectrum of opinion amongst the various madhahib, and each madhhab has a specific way of doing it. But you're emailing me, so I will give you a simple method, with the caveat that if you want to follow a madhhab strictly, then you should ask your particular scholar of the madhhab. What I'm telling you is basically one of the main or famous positions of the Hanbali madhhab. One of my teachers wrote an entire treatise on this, and he combined all the evidences, and this is what I'm presenting to you. So this is one opinion out of many.

How does one do sajdat al-sahw, the prostrations of forgetfulness? Now, when is it done? The prostration of forgetfulness is done for one of three reasons.

Number one, you forgot something that is a wajib. If you forget a sunnah, there is no sajdat al-sahw. If you forget to recite a surah after al-Fatiha, no sajdat al-sahw. If you forget a rukn, then you need to go back and do that rukn; you cannot do sajdat al-sahw. But if you forget a wajib accidentally: for example, sitting down in the second rak'ah out of three or four rak'ahs, and instead of sitting down, you stood up. Or when you went into sajdah and your mind was preoccupied and you didn't say "Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la"; you just went into sajdah, then you went back up, and then you realized, "Oh, I forgot to say Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la." So number one, if you forget a wajib, you can make it up with sajdat al-sahw.

Number two, when you add something that you should not have added, when you increase, when you do something you should not do. For example, you did a ruku', you went back up, and then you accidentally did another ruku'. Then you're like, "Oh, I already did the ruku'," but you've done it, so you did two ruku's in one rak'ah. Or you did a sajdah, and then, again, your mind is preoccupied, you did the second sajdah, then you did a third sajdah. Or, for example, you prayed four rak'at, and instead of sitting down on the fourth, you stood up and you finished a fifth rak'ah. So you added an entire rak'ah, and then you realized, "Oh, I added a rak'ah." So the second scenario is when you add something that you should not have added.

And the third scenario is when you are confused about how many rak'at you have prayed. You're in the third rak'ah or the second, and you're confused: is this the second or the third? Or is this the third or the fourth? And you really are unsure. So what do you do in that case? You choose the lesser of the two, that is, if you are totally unsure. If you think about it and you say, "Oh no, this is the third rak'ah," and you're fairly confident it's the third rak'ah (it's called ghalabat al-dhann), if you're pretty certain that it is the third rak'ah, then you go with it and you ignore the minor doubt. But if you're very uncertain or totally uncertain, in this case you will pray based upon the lower of the two. So if you're doubting between three and four, you will assume it's the third, you will pray as if it's the third, you will add a fourth, and then you will do sajdat al-sahw.

So to summarize, you do sajdat al-sahw, which is two sajdahs of forgetfulness, in one of three scenarios:

1. You forget a wajib accidentally. You will not forget a wajib intentionally, or else the prayer is invalid.
2. You add something to the salah that you should not have added: an extra rak'ah, an extra ruku', an extra sujud.
3. You are confused, and that confusion remains all the way to the end.

Now, another difference of opinion comes about: when does one do sajdat al-sahw? Do you do it after the taslim or before the taslim? And again, all of the madhhabs have their position, so feel free to ask a particular scholar. But if you're asking me, which you obviously are, since you're emailing me: **if you are confused, or if you have forgotten something, in these two cases the sajdah is done before the taslim.** So if you are confused between three and four, or if you missed a wajib (you didn't sit down for the second rak'ah and you stood up), in both of these situations you will continue to the end. You're sitting for the tahiyyah. Then, before you finish the salah, you will do two sajdahs immediately: "Allahu Akbar," go down, back up; "Allahu Akbar," go down, back up. Two. And then you will not repeat the tahiyyah and the salah upon the Prophet ﷺ; you will just do the taslim. So if you are confused about the number of rak'at, or if you forgot a wajib accidentally, then you do two sajdahs before the taslim.

And by the way, this is based on the hadith that the Prophet once prayed Dhuhr and he stood up in the second rak'ah and did not sit down, and all the people stood up with him. And when they sat down for the fourth rak'ah, the Prophet ﷺ went into sajdah twice, and then he did the taslim. So the people did sajdah twice and did the taslim. This shows that he stood up in the second rak'ah and did not sit down, and that is a wajib. And because he missed a wajib accidentally, he did sajdat al-sahw.

In another hadith as well, the Prophet ﷺ said: "If one of you is in doubt about his salah, and he doesn't know how much he has prayed, three or four, then get rid of the doubt and base what you have upon certainty, and then perform two sajdahs before you do the taslim." So get rid of the doubt and base it on certainty. Which of the two is more certain? It's going to be the lower of the two numbers. So out of three and four, three is certain and four is uncertain. So you go on the three, you ignore the four, you finish, and then you do two sajdahs.

As for if you have added: this happened once in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, that he accidentally prayed Dhuhr as two rak'at. And when he said the taslim, he turned around, and everybody did not know what to do. Some people thought that the salah had been shortened to two. So one person stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, did you make a mistake? Was it an error? Did you forget? Or is Salat al-Dhuhr now two rak'ahs?" And so the Prophet confirmed, "Did I pray two rak'ahs?" And they said yes. So he said, "I am a person like the rest of you. I forget like you forget." So he literally explained, "I am a human being, and I forget like you forget." And he then stood up and prayed two rak'at, and he did the taslim, then he made two sajdahs at the end, and then he did the taslim. So in this case, he did the sajdahs after the taslim. And this shows us that when you add something more... and in this case there was also a gap between the two and the two, and so he added the two taslims the first time. Then he prayed the two rak'at, and he did sajdat al-sahw.

So the bottom line is that there is a diversity of opinions. And really, the main point is that sajdat al-sahw is done for one of three reasons. As long as you remember that... to be very pedantic and technical, if you do all of them before the taslim, inshallah it will be accepted by Allah. Whether you do it before the taslim or after the taslim, that's really where a lot of difference of opinion comes amongst the four madhhabs. But don't worry about this. Just follow what is easy for you. You've asked a scholar; this is the position that I've told you to follow, so stick with it unless and until you study more. And Allah knows best.
